sections.overview: The Walleye Surfperch is an eastern Pacific surfperch in Embiotocidae. Its family relative Hypsurus caryi uses rocky shores and kelp edges more often.
sections.identification: It reaches about 30 cm, with a dark blue back, silver sides and narrow golden bars in juveniles.
sections.habitat: It ranges from Vancouver Island to central Baja, often in sandy surf near rocks or piers.
sections.behavior: It forms large schools and is a recreational fishery species.
sections.reproduction: Females carry developing young and usually bear five to twelve.
sections.ecology: It uses sandy surf as well as areas near rocks and piers.
sections.conservation: California monitoring describes substantial recreational catches, but the cited sources do not establish a global population trend.
